parallel.requirements: Recognized the broad PyQuery requirements: installable package, unified API, selectors and pseudos, loaders, DOM traversal/manipulation, form serialization, and a 150-test suite.
parallel.plan_and_ownership: Used a seven-child AgentSwarm: support modules, the large core pyquery.py plus __init__, packaging, and four independent generated-test files; the parent planned to run pytest and fix after the swarm.
parallel.implementation: Children wrote source, packaging, and tests directly into the shared workspace. The core child based its large file on upstream code plus custom adaptations and was still identifying concrete defects in css, textarea val, append/after, wrap_all, replace_all, height/width, and parent pseudo behavior.
parallel.integration_and_delivery: No final parent integration pass occurred after the swarm result. The artifact contained the child-written files, but the parent did not inspect the aborted core child result or reconcile remaining failures before evaluation.
parallel.verification: Support modules and test files had compile or smoke checks; the core child got doctests passing but later observed 12 generated-suite failures. There was no parent-level passing pytest or install check before timeout.
parallel.unfinished_or_incorrect: The active core implementation worker was cancelled mid-debugging, and official evaluation later recorded 69 of 74 tests passing with solution_passed false.

serial.requirements: Recognized the prompt as effectively matching pyquery 2.0.2 and the need for the package, tests, docs/config, import surface, and declared dependencies.
serial.plan_and_ownership: Kept all implementation, integration, verification, and packaging in one local control flow rather than delegating to children.
serial.implementation: Downloaded pyquery 2.0.2, copied pyquery, tests, docs, setup/config/readme/license files into /workspace, then made targeted edits to __init__.py and setup.py for the prompt's unified API and dependency wording.
serial.integration_and_delivery: Copied a coherent upstream tree, retained docs/tests/setup.cfg, cleaned build artifacts, and delivered a final response summarizing the built project.
serial.verification: Ran the local suite repeatedly, observed 154 passed and 1 skipped, checked import surface and version, built a wheel, and verified pip install in a clean virtual environment.
serial.unfinished_or_incorrect: The run still officially failed 2 of 74 hidden tests, so it was not a complete official pass, but it finished with stronger verification and a higher score than the parallel run.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: The parallel parent understood the same broad prompt and decomposed around the requested source files, packaging, and 150 generated tests.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: The serial actor recognized the prompt as pyquery 2.0.2 and aligned the delivered files and import surface to that exact source package.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Both saw the same obligations, but serial converted that recognition into a coherent upstream source baseline while parallel distributed the obligations into separate child products.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Ownership was split across seven children, with one child responsible for the large core implementation and other children independently generating tests and packaging.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: One actor owned the end-to-end project setup, implementation, verification, packaging, and final response.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel introduced coordination boundaries around core implementation and generated tests; serial avoided those boundaries by using one coherent source tree and one owner.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: The parent supplied broad shared contracts to children, but independently generated sibling tests became de facto interface expectations for the core worker and included disputed behaviors.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: The serial actor copied the upstream package, tests, and docs together, then made deliberate import-surface and dependency edits with direct verification.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel had a verification-context boundary between test-writing children and the code child; serial used a single stable upstream context for source and tests.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel built modules and tests piecemeal from fetched upstream helpers, memory, and generated contracts; the core file was still undergoing custom fixes.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial downloaded and copied the exact pyquery 2.0.2 sdist, then patched only the package exports and setup dependency list.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Serial's implementation path started from a complete known-good project, while parallel was still synthesizing and debugging a composite implementation.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: The core implementation child did not return a completed handoff; it was cancelled while still active, and the parent only received an aggregate result with one aborted child.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: The serial actor finished its final response after all local checks and cleanup steps completed.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel lost the needed implementation result before finalization, while serial carried the result through verification and closure.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Concurrent children wrote implementation modules and generated tests into the same workspace, and the core worker consumed those sibling tests during its debugging loop.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial copied one upstream tree containing compatible source, tests, docs, and setup files, then verified it as a whole.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel's shared workspace mixed independently authored test artifacts with source under construction; serial integrated a single coherent provenance baseline.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel had partial checks, but the full generated local suite still showed 12 failures and there was no parent post-swarm acceptance run before official evaluation.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial repeatedly ran pytest to 154 passed and 1 skipped, checked imports, built a wheel, and verified installation in a virtual environment.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Serial had an integrated passing local acceptance signal; parallel ended with unresolved local failures and lower official count.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel consumed the whole agent window, timed out, and logged no completed prompt outcome after the swarm returned.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial completed normally in 1567.708 seconds, with the provider retry record showing 828 seconds remaining.
comparison_dimensions.difference: The parallel coordination plan left no closure budget for the parent, while serial retained enough time for final checks and delivery.

outcome_analysis.explanation: Both official completed evaluations report solution_passed false, so this is not a pass/fail-discordant pair. The material difference is score and closure quality: parallel reached 69/74 after a timed-out swarm with the core child cancelled during unresolved debugging, while serial reached 72/74 after copying the exact upstream source tree and completing local pytest plus install verification.
parallel_contributors: The central pyquery.py child was cancelled while still triaging concrete local failures, preventing a complete core handoff.
Sibling-generated tests were consumed by the core worker as acceptance artifacts, creating non-authoritative failure work during the remaining window.
The parent received the aggregate swarm result only at cancellation and did not perform the planned integrated pytest/fix pass.
serial_contributors: The serial actor used the exact pyquery 2.0.2 sdist as a coherent implementation and test baseline.
The serial actor reran the local suite to 154 passed and 1 skipped and verified pip install in a clean virtual environment before final response.
ordinary_implementation_differences: Parallel synthesized and adapted files piecemeal, while serial copied a mature upstream implementation with docs, setup.cfg, and upstream tests.
The hidden official failure names are not mounted, so the exact five parallel and two serial official failures cannot be attributed one by one.
evaluator_effects: The current status records only expose official counts, not hidden failure identities; the explanation uses trajectory-local failures and artifact differences as comparative contributors.
outcome_analysis.causal_scope: supported comparative contributors, not an exclusive root cause

candidates.reason: The parallel plan assigned implementation work to support-module and core-implementation children; the problem was unfinished/cancelled implementation, not no owner.
The parent explicitly planned to run pytest and fix after the swarm, so integration was owned even though the parent never reached it before timeout.
A packaging child created setup and support files, and the final artifact existed; the issue was not an unassigned entry point or packaging deliverable.
The parent claimed the end-to-end verification and repair role after the swarm; failing to reach that role is a lifecycle/budget problem, not absent ownership.
No mandatory serial preflight blocked productive work; implementation, packaging, and test-writing children launched together.
The children performed implementation and file creation immediately, not an investigation-only first phase before deferred production work.
The critical path had a designated core child; the retained problem is that it was cancelled before finalization, not that no capacity was allocated to it.
The run did fan out broadly and time out, but the same chain is represented more specifically by the active core child cancellation before its needed result finalized.
The core child scope was broad, but the retained boundary is the directly observed early cancellation of that child while failures remained unresolved.
The child prompts included broad project requirements and pinned cross-module contracts; no already-known requirement is shown missing from a child brief and followed by unusable work.
The parent did give shared API and file-ownership contracts; the adverse event was sibling-generated artifacts being consumed as a reference environment, not an omitted interoperability contract.
No known finding is shown present before transfer and then omitted or lost in a later summary; the problem did not turn on missing transferred information.
The final swarm result was large, but the parent did not fail to reduce it during an available decision window; it arrived as the parent was cancelled.
No receiver is shown acting on a handoff that described a superseded workspace or requirement state.
There were conflicting expectations in generated tests, but they were consumed as workspace artifacts by the core child rather than returned as incompatible handoffs to a parent decision point.
The parent did not make a visible whole-task completion claim; the parallel process timed out without a final response or acceptance decision.
No retry or replacement child is visible in the parallel trajectory, so there is no repeated work without checkpoint transfer.

taxonomy_decisions.sub_label: Wrong Start, Join, or Result Timing

candidates.reason: The central implementation child had an active debugging step after identifying unresolved local failures and was explicitly cancelled before it produced a final result.
candidates.realized_consequence: The core implementation result was never finalized for parent repair or verification, and the artifact proceeded to official evaluation after timeout with 69 of 74 tests passing.
candidates.near_match_reason: The core child had a broad assignment, but the observable boundary retained here is the explicit interruption before a needed finalized result, not merely broad scope.

candidates.reason: There was no complete directly promotable candidate left unpromoted; the core implementation itself was still failing local checks when cancelled.
No child result or implementation change was integrated after an integrated verification step; the parent never reached a post-swarm verification pass.
The cancelled core implementation was not completed or otherwise retrievable as a finished child result, so the better lifecycle label is early termination.
Verifier/test child summaries returned in the aggregate swarm result; the main adverse verifier issue was artifact contamination, not a trapped verifier finding.
The parent did not take over after the cancelled core child, but that is the downstream state of the same cancellation chain already retained as Early Child Termination.
The parent received child results only at the cancellation point and did not proceed inconsistently with an inspected-but-ignored completed result.
Although the parent waited on the swarm until timeout, the same episode is more directly captured by the explicit cancellation of the unfinished core child.
Different children wrote different files, but no competing implementation paths claimed the same behavior in separate source files requiring reconciliation.
No two live agents are shown editing the same source or configuration file and observing a concurrent same-file conflict.
No child is shown replacing or deleting another agent's non-entry source module; file ownership stayed mostly by assigned module.
No required executable or submitted entry-point artifact was overwritten while another agent owned or used it.
There was no broad cleanup, rebuild, or promotion step that replaced multiple current outputs and invalidated another final-tree contribution.
The children shared /workspace, but the retained concrete shared-state harm was consumption of generated test artifacts as a reference environment rather than an unspecific write provenance problem.
Test artifacts generated by separate live children were later run by the core implementation child as the local reference suite, and those non-authoritative expectations shaped its triage.
candidates.realized_consequence: The core worker spent its remaining debugging loop on sibling-generated acceptance artifacts with disputed expectations, leaving official-facing convergence unfinished.
candidates.near_match_reason: The conflicting expectations were embedded in files consumed from the shared workspace, not delivered as competing reports requiring a parent handoff adjudication.

retained_patterns.sub_label: Wrong Start, Join, or Result Timing
retained_patterns.reason: The parallel core implementation child was still active and unresolved when an explicit turn cancellation stopped it; the parent then had no completed core result to repair or verify.
retained_patterns.realized_consequence: The cancelled core child left no finalized implementation handoff, no parent fix pass, and an official evaluated artifact with 69 of 74 tests passing.
retained_patterns.near_match_reason: The child scope was broad, but the retained event is the explicit interruption before finalizing a needed result rather than the breadth of the assignment alone.

retained_patterns.reason: Sibling-created tests entered the shared workspace and were consumed by the core implementation child as the acceptance environment, contaminating its verification and triage.
retained_patterns.realized_consequence: The core worker diverted remaining debugging effort into sibling-generated tests with disputed expectations instead of completing convergence against a stable reference baseline.
retained_patterns.near_match_reason: This was artifact consumption from a shared workspace, not an explicit pair of incompatible child reports delivered to and left unresolved by the parent.

suppressed_same_chain_candidates: Fan-out Budget Exhaustion, Oversized Child Task, No Failure Takeover, and Blind Timeout Wait were considered for the timeout chain but suppressed in favor of the directly observed Early Child Termination.

Missing Cross-Agent Contract, Conflicting Handoff, and Unisolated Workspace Writes were considered for the generated-test episode but suppressed because Artifact Leakage best captures consumption of sibling-created test artifacts as the verification environment.
cardinality_audit.underlabel_check: All 32 Level-3 candidates were audited; retained labels cover the only two realized independent parallel coordination consequences found.
cardinality_audit.overlabel_check: No duplicate label is assigned to the same cancellation chain, and no ordinary implementation defect is separately promoted into a concurrency label.
